reconciled_note: A full list_triggers reading, the first since 2026-08-09T09:11Z — seventeen hours. It found TWO enabled hourly claude-trigger rows that this registry did not contain at all, both created within the hour before it was read (01:32Z and 01:57Z). pacing.mjs reserves the weekly pool per enabled row, so for those minutes the gate was dividing the pool among two other loops when there were four. This is the same class of error as the revenue-loop row that stayed enabled after the owner stopped it and reserved 9.43% for a trigger that could not fire, except in the direction that says there is MORE room than there is. Only a lap with MCP can take this reading; Actions has no access to the scheduler API. The listing was paginated (has_more true) — the fifty most recent were read, which covers every trigger created since 2026-07-22, and forty-five of them are spent one-shot send_later rows.

automations.note: Spends the Codex weekly pool, which is separate from the Claude window and was sitting at 100% unused on 2026-08-09 because nothing dispatched it. The mouth is codex/INBOX.md; scripts/inbox-task.mjs decides whether the task is live and unmarked before any model runs. Hourly since 2026-08-09: the daily cron had delivered zero runs in the workflow's entire history — all ten were workflow_dispatch — so an external answer arrived only when a lap happened to have MCP tools, and that is the lane the whole route depends on. 2026-08-10: the pool this row calls separate and unused is actually TWO weekly windows, and only one was reachable — codex exec with no --model runs the account default, so GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark stayed at 100% for this lane's entire history while being cited as spare capacity. The dispatch now names a model derived from the meter (scripts/spark-model.mjs) and falls back to the default if refused; scripts/spark-model.mjs --check runs in pulse.yml so it cannot quietly go back to unnamed.

liveness.note: Moved off state/answers/latest.json when the cron went hourly. That file only moves when a question is actually put to the model, and a healthy hourly lane skips most of its runs because the task already carries its done marker — so keyed on the answer, an idle lane and a stopped lane look the same. scripts/record-lane-run.mjs stamps checked_at on every run including the skips, which is the mark that dates the SCHEDULE rather than the product.
